title: GroundTruth — Understand your code. Think in systems.
evidenceLabel: Edited walkthrough · real hosted UI captures · synthetic demo account

scenes.title: Understand the system. Try the next change.
scenes.caption: A learning path for builders. Evidence for teachers.
scenes.narration: AI can build a working app before its builder understands the system. GroundTruth helps the learner understand code and architecture, then practise the next change independently.

scenes.title: Make independent understanding easier to inspect
scenes.caption: A polished take-home artifact is only part of the assessment story.
scenes.narration: Teachers face a connected problem. A polished, AI-assisted take-home artifact can conceal gaps in independent understanding. Responsible AI learners also need a fair chance to demonstrate ability. Reconstructing missing reasoning can add manual marking work. This edited walkthrough uses real interface captures and synthetic demo data.

scenes.title: Start with a feature, before a filename
scenes.caption: Choose the workflow you want to understand.
scenes.narration: Start with a public repository and a feature. The learner chooses a backend workflow in our small study-task app, before needing to know a filename.

scenes.title: Connect code to system responsibilities
scenes.caption: Follow a request through validation and persistence.
scenes.narration: The overview connects selected source to system responsibilities. Where does a request go? Which component validates it? A reading flow and glossary help the learner build that mental model.

scenes.title: Find a shared concept to investigate
scenes.caption: Use concept-linked evidence to focus the next discussion.
scenes.narration: The concept tree links those responsibilities to focused practice. It also gives teacher and learner a shared concept to discuss, rather than relying only on the finished artifact.

scenes.title: Ask about this code, rather than grade an artifact
scenes.caption: Dynamic practice questions. No automatic artifact grading.
scenes.narration: Muse Spark generates code-linked MCQs and tiny coding tasks. The question responds to the source and goal. This is contextual practice, not AI grading of a take-home project. Suggested answers still need source review.

scenes.title: Protect an explicit independent attempt
scenes.caption: Study help pauses. The original response is retained.
scenes.narration: During an independent attempt, new study assistance pauses. The original submitted response is preserved before feedback. The learner may also end the attempt. GroundTruth cannot prevent outside help or infer authorship.

scenes.title: Give the teacher context beyond the artifact
scenes.caption: Original attempts and observed app activity, shared by choice.
scenes.narration: The learner chooses what to share. Original attempts and observed activity add context for review. The concept index is provisional evidence, not a grade. These synthetic records are not learning-effectiveness results.

scenes.title: Inspect the answer. Choose a fresh follow-up.
scenes.caption: Review now. Teacher quiz authoring and cohort analytics are future work.
scenes.narration: The teacher can inspect the original answer and identify a concept worth a fresh unaided follow-up. This can inform teaching, while judgement stays human. Teacher AI quiz authoring, assignment distribution and cohort analytics remain future work.

scenes.title: Responsible AI learning. Human judgement.
scenes.caption: Understand the system. Try independently. Make the evidence inspectable.
scenes.narration: Meta provides contextual content. GroundTruth on Vercel controls access and learning state, with Supabase preserving evidence. Support responsible AI learning. Understand the system, try independently, and make the evidence inspectable.
